subject: Reasoning
topic: Course of Action — Problem and Response Questions (Set W7)

questions.stem:
Read the problem statement and decide which course(s) of action logically follow:

Problem: Traffic congestion has become severe in the city due to a rapidly growing number of vehicles.
Course of Action I: The government should build more flyovers and widen roads.
Course of Action II: Stricter traffic management rules and enforcement should be implemented.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both courses of action are practical and address the problem. Building infrastructure (I) expands road capacity. Strict enforcement (II) improves traffic flow. Both together form a comprehensive solution to urban traffic congestion.

questions.stem:
Problem: A fire broke out in a factory at night, and several workers are reported missing.
Course of Action I: The factory should be shut down permanently as it is a safety risk.
Course of Action II: Rescue teams should be immediately deployed to search for the missing workers.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: B is correct. The immediate priority is to save lives — deploying rescue teams (II) is urgent and appropriate. Permanently shutting down the factory (I) is premature and extreme without an investigation. A more proportionate response would be a temporary shutdown followed by an inquiry. Only II is a direct and justified response.

questions.stem:
Problem: Road accident fatalities in the state have increased by 30% this year.
Course of Action I: Intensive road safety awareness campaigns should be organised.
Course of Action II: Penalties for traffic rule violations such as speeding and drunk driving should be made more stringent.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both courses of action directly address road safety. Awareness campaigns (I) educate people. Stricter penalties (II) deter dangerous driving behaviour. A rise in fatalities warrants both education and enforcement — they complement each other.

questions.stem:
Problem: Many students from rural areas drop out of school before completing secondary education due to financial hardship.
Course of Action I: The government should expand scholarship schemes and mid-day meal programmes in rural schools.
Course of Action II: Private schools in cities should be legally required to donate 50% of their seats to rural students.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: A is correct. Course I (scholarships + mid-day meals) directly addresses financial barriers to rural education — it is practical and targeted. Course II is impractical and does not address the problem: forcing city private schools to reserve seats for rural students involves logistics (transport, relocation) that are not feasible for young students. Only I follows.

questions.stem:
Problem: Stray dog attacks have increased significantly in urban areas, causing injuries to pedestrians.
Course of Action I: All stray dogs in the city should be captured and humanely relocated to shelters.
Course of Action II: Citizens should be fined for feeding stray dogs in public places.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both measures address the stray dog menace. Sheltering dogs (I) reduces their number on streets and addresses their welfare. Limiting public feeding (II) prevents congregation and habituation of dogs in certain areas. Together these measures reduce the attack risk.

questions.stem:
Problem: Prices of essential commodities like onions have doubled in the last month due to poor harvest.
Course of Action I: The government should print more currency to help citizens afford food.
Course of Action II: The government should ban the export of all food items immediately.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: D is correct. Printing more currency (I) causes inflation — it would make prices rise further, not fall. Banning ALL food exports (II) is disproportionate; a blanket ban would harm the economy and trade relations. More appropriate actions would be importing commodities or releasing buffer stocks. Neither extreme measure logically follows.

questions.stem:
Problem: Digital literacy among India's workforce is low, limiting employment opportunities in the technology sector.
Course of Action I: Computer education should be made compulsory from Class 6 in all government schools.
Course of Action II: Free digital literacy training centres should be established in rural areas.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both courses address digital literacy gaps. Mandatory school-level computer education (I) addresses the next generation. Rural training centres (II) address the current adult workforce immediately. Both are necessary for a comprehensive response.

questions.stem:
Problem: A student was caught cheating in a public examination.
Course of Action I: The student's paper should be cancelled and they should be barred from the examination for one year.
Course of Action II: The examination hall should be closed for the day and all other students should be sent home.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: A is correct. Cancelling the offending student's paper and a temporary ban (I) is a proportionate, standard response to exam cheating. Closing the entire hall (II) punishes innocent students — this is disproportionate. The guilty party alone should face consequences. Only I follows.

questions.stem:
Problem: A study found that 40% of employees in large corporations experience severe burnout and stress.
Course of Action I: Companies should be mandated by law to provide paid mental health days in addition to regular leave.
Course of Action II: Employees should be encouraged to take up yoga and meditation on their own time.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: B is correct. Mandating paid mental health leave (I) is a significant policy intervention that requires extensive legislative groundwork — it does not necessarily 'follow' as an immediate course of action from the finding. Encouraging wellness practices (II) is a reasonable, immediately actionable response that companies can implement now. In exam reasoning, 'follows' means logically practical and proportionate. Only II qualifies here.

questions.stem:
Problem: A newly opened restaurant failed its health and hygiene inspection due to critically unsanitary kitchen conditions.
Course of Action I: The restaurant should be served an immediate closure notice and given 30 days to rectify conditions before re-inspection.
Course of Action II: The restaurant should be allowed to continue serving customers while it works on improving hygiene standards.

options.option_text: Only Course of Action I follows
Only Course of Action II follows
Both Courses of Action I and II follow
Neither Course of Action follows

questions.explanation: A is correct. When a food establishment fails a health inspection due to critical sanitary conditions, public safety requires immediate closure — allowing it to continue (II) risks customer health. Closure with a remediation period (I) is the balanced, proportionate, and standard regulatory response. Only I follows.
